grh_dd81e273088d3bd8cfa1.title: The Accident
paragraphs: Dr. Christian attends the twenty-fifth anniversary celebration of admired former governor Charles Van Ness and his wife Carolyn, a couple everyone in Rivers End regards as an ideal marriage. Charlie leaves the party on a winter night and is killed when his car skids on a mountain road. After Christian brings the news home, Carolyn finally admits that the public image was false: she had repeatedly protected Charlie's reputation and hidden how unhappy their marriage really was. Returning to the crash scene, Christian finds that Charlie apparently swerved to avoid Cliff Peters, the town drunk, who is also found dead nearby. Everyone expects Cliff's wife Ellen to feel relieved to be free of him, but she remembers a very different man, a loving husband and father whose kindness the town never saw. The two deaths overturn Rivers End's easy judgments about both marriages and leave Christian reflecting on how little outsiders can truly know about another person's love.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on November 15, 1938. It is listed as episode 30 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Lou Merrill, Myra Marsh, and Ynez Seabury. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_ddbf0ffb3e4b98e62aca.title: Spiral Staircase
paragraphs: Traumatized by witnessing her parents' deaths, Helen has been unable to speak for years and works in the Warren household while a killer stalks women he considers physically imperfect. During a storm, suspicion seems to point toward volatile Steven Warren, but Helen discovers that the apparently respectable professor is the murderer and that he has deliberately used Steven's presence to divert suspicion. Trapped in the house and targeted because of her muteness, Helen races up and down the spiral staircase trying to reach Mrs. Warren's gun. Mrs. Warren finally shoots the killer, and the shock breaks Helen's silence: she is able to telephone Dr. Perry herself and speak for the first time since childhood.

Other credited names include Milton Geiger as radio adaptor and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.

grh_ddeef0f757cf940fe712.title: Body and Soul
paragraphs: Charlie Davis rises from neighborhood boxer to champion, but success ties him to promoter Roberts and a corrupt fight business that treats fighters as disposable assets. After an opponent with a known brain injury dies following a rigged bout, Charlie finally understands the human cost of the racket, even as Roberts arranges for him to throw his own title fight. Given $60,000 to bet against himself, Charlie instead fights to win, rejecting the fix and Roberts' control. He leaves the ring bruised but morally free, reunited with Peg and declaring that Roberts can no longer take anything from him.

grh_dd0f6f9f11309f4b28d9.title: I'm Sorry, Mom
paragraphs: Resentful rich kid Jerry arranges his own fake kidnapping with a group of criminals, expecting his mother to pay a $100,000 ransom that he and the gang can divide. The supposed accomplices turn the scheme real: they assault Jerry's mother when she brings the money, set her adrift and decide to keep the entire ransom. Jerry finally understands that his mother risked herself because she loves him and tries to back out, but the gang has no reason to leave a witness. His mother survives long enough to alert authorities, while Jerry's attempt to punish her ends with his own death.

paragraphs: Navy sailors Joe and Pip miss their train after Joe jumps off in Rivers End chasing a woman he mistakes for an old sweetheart.
